# Golden fixtures

This directory holds golden-file test cases for `tests/test_golden.py`: real
(or synthetic) meshes with hand-verified expected extraction output, checked
directly into the mesh so a change to the extraction algorithm that shifts
results is caught by CI, not discovered later on a real customer scan.

## Provenance and consent

Every real scan checked in here is sensitive personal data (see CLAUDE.md
gotcha #5: scans are body scans, likely of minors). Before adding a real
scan fixture:

- Log the capture and hand-tape-measure comparison in
  `docs/accuracy-log.md` first. That file is the provenance and consent
  record for every fixture in this directory; a fixture with no matching
  entry there should not exist.
- Confirm the entry's "Consent" field says fixture-eligible, not just
  "captured". Consent to be measured is not the same as consent to have the
  mesh committed to a git repository.
- Keep the mesh small (crop to just the leg, decimate if needed) and
  anonymized (no face, no identifying background, no metadata).

Synthetic fixtures (generated geometry, no human subject) have no consent
requirement and are the preferred way to add golden coverage for a specific
algorithm edge case.

## Convention

Each golden case is a matched pair of files sharing a `<name>`:

- `<name>.obj` (or `.ply` / `.glb`): the mesh, loaded the same way the
  pipeline loads any untrusted upload (`zells_pipeline.extraction.mesh_loading.load_mesh`).
- `<name>.expected.json`: the expected output, shaped as:

  ```json
  {
    "values": {
      "Leg_Length": 350.0,
      "S1_ISW": 40.0,
      "...": "... all 25 keys from the frozen measurement schema ..."
    },
    "tolerances": {
      "S2_ICD": {"pct": 5.0, "abs_mm": 2.0}
    }
  }
  ```

  `values` must contain all 25 keys from `packages/shared/schema/measurements.schema.json`.

  `tolerances` is optional and per-key: omit it entirely, or omit any key
  within it, to use the suite-wide default tolerance (see
  `DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_PCT` / `DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_ABS_MM` in
  `tests/test_golden.py`): 2% relative or 1.0mm absolute, whichever is
  larger. Override `pct` and/or `abs_mm` per key for dimensions known to be
  noisier (e.g. a depth measurement on a mesh with a rough section).

`tests/test_golden.py` auto-discovers every `<name>.expected.json` with a
matching mesh file in this directory and runs one parametrized comparison
per pair. If this directory has no fixture pairs, that test module reports
as **skipped** (not silently passed) so an empty suite is never mistaken for
a green one.

## Generating the `expected.json` for a new fixture

Never hand-type the 25 expected values. Run the real extraction once against
the mesh (with `--json`, via the CLI in `zells_pipeline.extract`, or a short
script) and use its `values` output as the starting point, then adjust only
after hand-verifying against a tape measure and logging the comparison in
`docs/accuracy-log.md`.

## The synthetic case

`synthetic-frustum.obj` / `synthetic-frustum.expected.json` are generated by
`scripts/make_synthetic_fixture.py`, which builds the same tapered-ellipse
frustum used by `tests/conftest.py` (imported from there, not duplicated)
and writes its expected values by running the real extraction against it.
Regenerate both files by re-running that script if the frustum's
constructed dimensions in `tests/conftest.py` ever change.
